clue.text: Vigil kept by every member of the force

definitions.text: Vigil kept by every member of the force

parts.words: Vigil kept by every member of the force
parts.note: a period of keeping guard, the duty every constable does on the beat, and the old name for the night police themselves

explanation.surface: Every police officer takes a turn at staying up on guard through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a spell of staying awake on guard, which is what a sentry or constable does on duty.

clue.text: Look-out man on Boxing Day

parts.note: the carol tells of a good king who looked out on the Feast of Stephen, the day after Christmas

explanation.surface: A sentry stands guard on the day after Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day, 26 December, is the Feast of Stephen in the carol 'Good King Wenceslas looked out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's good king looked out on the Feast of Stephen, which falls on December 26.

clue.text: Moulding the bull, say ?

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken and we take what it sounds like

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone shapes a figure of a bull in clay.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture this is a convex ring-shaped moulding at the base of a column.

clue.text: Hunting pink — Tally ho! After him!

definitions.text: Hunting pink — Tally ho! After him!

parts.words: Hunting pink — Tally ho! After him!
parts.note: the pink is a colour and tally-ho a call, and 'After him!' is the shout of pursuit

explanation.surface: A huntsman in scarlet coat shouts as the fox breaks cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunting pink is the red coat of foxhunters; tally-ho is their cry on sighting the fox.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outcry raised in pursuit of a criminal, once a legal duty on all who heard it.

clue.text: Milton's girl in all is sportive

definitions.text: Milton's girl in all is sportive

parts.words: Milton's girl in all is sportive
parts.note: recalls the line in Milton's Lycidas about sporting with a shepherdess in the shade

explanation.surface: A poet's sweetheart is playful in everything she does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in all is' looks like anagram fodder but cannot give nine letters; the clue alludes to Lycidas: 'To sport with Amaryllis in the shade'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is the shepherdess Milton names in Lycidas as the girl one might sport with.

clue.text: A large sloth many recognize as Anne's favourite

parts.note: big means large
an ai is a three-toed sloth
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a good number

explanation.surface: Lots of people see a big lazy creature as the queen's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: Abigail Masham was the favourite of Queen Anne; 'recognize as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail Masham was the court favourite who supplanted the Duchess of Marlborough with Queen Anne.

clue.text: Forgetting a name is awkward

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so the letters are placed in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Not remembering someone's name is embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is A NAME plus IS; 'awkward' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the state of not remembering.

clue.text: Upset, love? Oh, yes The brute!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the run of words is turned bottom to top

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
ay is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A lover is upset, cries 'Oh yes!' and calls him a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns O + OH + AY to read upwards; the brutes are the beastly humans of Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swift's Gulliver's Travels these are the degraded human-like beasts, hence any boorish lout.

clue.text: One who washes a linen frock, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken and the sound matched

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen, so a linen frock is a lawn dress

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a linen dress does the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to wash and iron clothes and linen.

clue.text: Strangers thus observed at Westminster

parts.note: the Commons formula 'I spy strangers' is how a member asked for visitors to be cleared

explanation.surface: Visitors are watched closely in the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the British Parliament; strangers are members of the public in the gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I spy strangers' in the House of Commons demanded the public be removed, so strangers were seen this way.

clue.text: One raw gin fuddled a North countryman

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled by drink, so the letters of the three words are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: A northerner gets tipsy on a single neat gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuddled' rearranges ONE RAW GIN; 'North countryman' suggests a northern Englishman but means a man from Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Norway is literally a man from a northern country.

clue.text: Islam's lunch-time beauty?

parts.note: lunch-time is one o'clock, written as 'hour one' with the Roman numeral, and the beauty is the nymph of the Muslim paradise

explanation.surface: A lovely woman of the Muslim world appears at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunch-time read as 'hour I', the hour one, spells the Islamic nymph of paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic belief a houri is one of the beautiful maidens awaiting the faithful in paradise.

clue.text: No end for a Jewish sectarian in German city

indicators.note: the sectarian loses the last letter, so the word is cut short at its tail

parts.note: an Essene was a member of an ascetic Jewish sect of Roman times

explanation.surface: A member of an ancient Jewish sect finds no rest in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr in western Germany.

clue.text: A science scholar, done wrong by many, ran off

parts.note: a BSc is a Bachelor of Science, a graduate scholar in science

indicators.note: done wrong means the letters of the word done are put out of order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: A science graduate, cheated by lots of people, did a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DONE as ONDE; 'by' is a link joining it to D for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave hurriedly and secretly, usually to escape something.

clue.text: Standing to reason government issue in the pub

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another, here the pub word holds the issue

parts.note: the local is a regular's neighbourhood pub
GI stands for government issue, the US term for army kit and soldiers

explanation.surface: A soldier in the bar is standing up to argue a point.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LOCAL is British slang for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stands to reason follows sensibly from the facts, which is rational thinking.

clue.text: Latin speech has this part for Amanda

definitions.text: Latin speech has this part for Amanda

parts.words: Latin speech has this part for Amanda
parts.note: the girl's name comes from a Latin verb form meaning 'she who must be loved', a part of speech

explanation.surface: A Latin play gives a role to a girl called Amanda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' means part of speech, not a role: amanda is the Latin verb form 'to be loved'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin verbal adjective expressing necessity, as amandus, 'fit to be loved'.

clue.text: Be he so ingenuous, it would be cruel

definitions.text: Be he so ingenuous, it would be cruel

parts.words: Be he so ingenuous, it would be cruel
parts.note: put 'he' in front of the word for ingenuous and it becomes a word for cruel

explanation.surface: If a man were really that naive, it would be unkind to exploit him.
explanation.walkthrough: The ingenuous word, preceded by HE, becomes HEARTLESS, meaning cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuous means innocent and guileless, free of craft or cunning.

clue.text: How fiery chariots cope with unseen difficulties

definitions.text: How fiery chariots cope with unseen difficulties

parts.words: How fiery chariots cope with unseen difficulties
parts.note: Elijah was carried to heaven in a chariot of fire, and schoolboys render unseen Latin passages into English

explanation.surface: Blazing war wagons deal with hidden obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: To be carried bodily to heaven, as Elijah was, is to be 'translated'; an unseen is a passage set for rendering in a language exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to render into another language and to convey bodily to heaven.

clue.text: Avoids the way up to the tradesmen's entrance

definitions.meaning: dodges, steps out of the way

definitions.text: the way up to the tradesmen's entrance
definitions.meaning: the stairs at the side of a house leading to the door used by delivery men

explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to move aside, and tradesmen once used the stairs at the flank of a house rather than the front door.

clue.text: Way two boys got lost?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Ray is a boy's name
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Which way did a pair of lads go when they went missing?
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the right path and so become lost.

clue.text: Rescind an amendment, see ?

indicators.note: an amendment changes something, so the letters of the word are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Cancel a change to the law, do you understand?
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or make out with the eyes or mind.

clue.text: Converted to meadow, as I told the cops

definitions.meaning: land sown with grass has been turned into pasture
in British slang to grass is to inform on someone to the police

explanation.definitionFit: Land laid down to pasture is sown with turf; an informer who reports to police is a supergrass in slang.

clue.text: Gregarious fish'?.

parts.note: a sociable creature might be called one that forms a crowd, which names a large sea fish

explanation.surface: A sea creature that likes to swim in company.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea bass of warm waters; read as 'one who forms a gang', it suits a sociable sort.

clue.text: Show cipher used in communist writing

parts.note: to manifest is to show or display
a cipher is a zero, the figure O

explanation.surface: A code is displayed in a piece of red propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' is a link; 'cipher' means nought here, not a code.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx and Engels wrote the Communist Manifesto, the founding pamphlet of the movement.

clue.text: End of Burton's pilgrimage

parts.note: the explorer Sir Richard Burton travelled in disguise to the holy city of Islam

explanation.surface: Where the explorer's journey of devotion came to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' suggests taking the last letter of Burton, but it means the destination.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy city of Islam, goal of the hajj, which Burton reached disguised in 1853.

clue.text: But more than 72 words in Shakespeare's first one

definitions.text: But more than 72 words in Shakespeare's first one

parts.words: But more than 72 words in Shakespeare's first one
parts.note: a legal document is measured in units of 72 words, and the 1623 collected plays were the first large-format edition

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's first collection held a great many more words than that.
explanation.walkthrough: In legal copying a folio is a unit of 72 (or 90) words; the First Folio of 1623 collected Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a 72-word unit of legal text and the large book format of 1623's collected plays.

clue.text: Girl is turned into boy

indicators.note: turned means the girl's name and the little word are read together backwards

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A girl undergoes a transformation and becomes a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' runs SALIS backwards; 'into' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Silas is a boy's name, as in George Eliot's Silas Marner.

clue.text: What's current in France? Nothing in another currency

indicators.note: in says the zero goes inside the Italian money

parts.note: lire were the Italian currency before the euro
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking about money in France brings an answer in a different coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' means a flowing stream, not money: France's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current of water, and this is the longest river in France.

clue.text: Cold, then hot, then laid up with this

definitions.text: Cold, then hot, then laid up with this

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
H is the abbreviation for hot on a tap
laid up means confined to bed, sick

explanation.surface: First shivering, then feverish, then bedridden by a mild illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes catching this ailment: shivers, fever, then bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A feverish cold with shivering fits is what people call catching a bad bout of the sniffles.

clue.text: Hemp possibly, with a glutinous additive for stress

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the plant fibre might be arranged another way

parts.note: size is a sticky glaze added to paper or plaster

explanation.surface: Cannabis, perhaps, mixed with gum to relieve tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HEMP as EMPH; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to give it special weight, to underline it.

clue.text: What's brewing? A sly look round the state shows him

indicators.note: round means the sly look encloses the state's abbreviation

parts.note: a leer is a sly or knowing look
Conn is the abbreviation for Connecticut, a US state

explanation.surface: A suspicious glance around the country reveals what's fermenting.
explanation.walkthrough: An ale-conner was an old borough official who tested what was brewing; 'shows him' points back to that question as his job.
explanation.definitionFit: The ale-conner inspected beer and ale for quality, asking of every brew whether it was fit to sell.

clue.text: Water-bearers get right among the sheep

indicators.note: among says the letter goes in the middle of the flock word

parts.note: ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Carriers of water go right in among the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug for carrying water.
